sources.obliquity_deg: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html (6.68 obliquity to orbit - 5.145 orbit inclination, Cassini state 2: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini%27s_laws; cross-check 1.5424 at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon)
sources.year_d: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon (draconic year 346.62 d; cf. 2 x 173.3 d in https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEhelp/moonorbit.html)

limitations: mean solar time (no equation of time)
Sun as a point, no refraction

spice_crosscheck.method: Hourly true Sun elevation from SPICE (de440s, IAU_EARTH / MOON_ME, LT+S) vs analytic model; analytic phase aligned once per body at SPICE northward equinox and per point at the t0 local hour angle, then free-running over one declination period from 2026-01-01T00:00:00 UTC.

site_finder.slope_constraint: p90 of the four 240 m LDSM slopes in each 480 m cell <= limit

diagnostic_sun_psr_vs_earth_zero.note: not a criterion: Earth shadows are displaced towards the Earth

alignment.revision_note: First run used 'sun PSR vs Earth-zero shift == 0' as a criterion; it gave (-3, 0). Debug pass showed the Earth-zero shift is towards the Earth (dc = 0, dr < 0) in all quadrants while sun PSRs match DEM lows with no shift, i.e. shadow geometry, not misalignment. Criterion replaced by the per-quadrant checks above. Weights unchanged.

layers_meta.aggregation: 2x2 blocks of 240 m pixels: mean (sun, earth, slope, elevation), p90 of the 4 slopes, min PSR distance, PSR pixel fraction

limitations: Sunlight and Earth visibility are averages over an 18.6-year cycle, not a specific mission date.
Grid cell 480 m; slopes are from a 240 m map, smoother than the 100 m landing-slope baseline.
Communication = line of sight to Earth only (no relay, antenna or link budget).
No thermal, dust or trafficability modelling.
Illumination and Earth-visibility layers are NASA LOLA team products (Mazarico et al. 2011), not our computation.

corpus.gsd_note: all bodies resampled to ~926 m (Earth has only ETOPO 2022 30" globally)

datasets.moon: LRO LOLA LDEM_64 (LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0), 2x2 block mean to 32 px/deg
datasets.moon_sp: LRO LOLA LDEM_60S_240MPP_ADJ south-polar stereographic, 4x4 block mean to 960 m
datasets.earth: NOAA NCEI ETOPO 2022 v1 30 arc-second surface elevation (ETOPO_2022_v1_30s_N90W180_surface)
datasets.mars: MGS MOLA DEM mosaic global 463 m (Mars_MGS_MOLA_DEM_mosaic_global_463m), 2x2 block mean

known_analog_test.method: percentile rank of each known analog site among all uniformly sampled Earth index points by terrain-feature distance to each target it is an analog for (0 % = best). Baseline: 1000 random Earth index points (seed 1000), each paired with a target drawn in turn from the same (site, target) list.

notes: McMurdo Dry Valleys (University Valley) are inside the Natural Earth 10 m 'Antarctic Ice Sheet' polygon, so the ice mask removes them; not evaluable with this mask.
Sites on narrow coasts or islands have no fully valid 12 km land window; they are snapped to the nearest valid Earth index point within 50 km (snapped_km, evaluated_at) or reported as not evaluable.
Analog sites were chosen by their operators for geology, climate or logistics; terrain shape at 926 m / 12 km is only one aspect, so poor ranks are expected for some (e.g. Rio Tinto).

multiscale_decision.rule_declared_before_run: switch current to v2 only if the known-analog median percentile (all pairs) improves by >= 5 points vs v1 AND the random baseline stays ~50 % AND find_twins p95 < 1 s; analog list and weights not tuned
caveats: v2 requires a fully valid 36 km window: 972,567 Earth points vs 1,026,242 in v1; coastal / island sites (Lanzarote, Bockfjorden) are not evaluable and small islands no longer appear as twins
median of per-site medians got worse (54.69 -> 57.97); the gain is in pairs, led by Haughton (63.09 -> 41.69)
v2 still does not rank known analogs clearly better than random points (51.12 % vs baseline 48.54 %)
